title: The Leg Day Recovery Routine I Wish I Knew Sooner
creator: Jess Tavares
description:
Everything I do after a heavy leg day so I can actually walk down the stairs on Thursday.

sentences.t: Okay, we just finished leg day, and I can already feel my quads filing a formal complaint.
Today was heavy squats, Romanian deadlifts, walking lunges, and then leg extensions until I wanted to cry.
And for years, this is the point where I'd just go home, eat whatever, and then be wrecked for three days.
So I want to show you the recovery routine I do now, because it's honestly changed how often I can train.
First up, the cooldown, and I know everyone skips it, I used to skip it.
It's just ten minutes on the bike at a really easy pace, like, conversation pace.
You're not trying to burn calories here, you're just getting blood moving through the legs.
Then I go straight to the floor for some mobility work.
Couch stretch, ninety seconds each side, and yes, it is horrible.
Then a deep goblet squat hold with a light weight, just sitting in the bottom and breathing.
And then pigeon pose for my glutes, because after Romanian deadlifts they are screaming.
Okay, step two is food, and this is where I was getting it really wrong.
I'd train hard and then eat a salad and wonder why I felt like garbage.
Now I aim for a proper meal within a couple of hours, with around forty grams of protein and a good amount of carbs.
Today that's rice, chicken thighs, and a mountain of roasted veg, plus a big glass of water with electrolytes.
Hydration is the most boring tip in the world and it still matters more than any supplement.
But none of that does much if you're sleeping five hours a night, and that's honestly how I ended up wearing this ring.
This is Nocto, and they're sponsoring today's video.
It's a sleep and recovery ring, so it tracks your sleep stages, your resting heart rate, and your heart rate variability overnight.
Every morning it gives you a recovery score, so on days when my body is clearly not ready, I swap the heavy session for something lighter.
The battery lasts about a week, it's way less annoying to sleep in than a watch, and there's no monthly subscription.
If you want one, head to nocto.com and use code JESS for fifty dollars off.
Okay, step three, the evening.
I do a short walk after dinner, maybe twenty minutes, and it is weirdly the best thing for next day soreness.
Then a hot shower, and some nights a few minutes with the foam roller on my quads and calves.
I don't go crazy with the roller, it's not a punishment, just a little light pressure.
Then screens off by about ten thirty and in bed, which, I know, sounds very grandma, but it works.
Step four is the next day, and this is the big mindset shift.
The day after legs I don't sit on the couch, I move.
An easy walk, some swimming if I can get to the pool, or another light spin on the bike.
Total rest actually makes me stiffer, light movement makes me recover faster.
And then I train upper body, so I'm not losing a training day while my legs come back.
So, to recap, cooldown, mobility, a real meal, water, a walk, sleep, and moving the next day.
None of it is fancy, and that's kind of the point.
If you've got a recovery trick I didn't mention, drop it in the comments, I read all of them.
And I'll see you on Thursday for upper body.
